PREPLANNING_CONTEXT: {"version":1,"schema_version":2,"epicId":"af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81","generatedAt":"2026-06-02T00:00:00Z","generatedBy":"preplanning","epic":{"title":"Make forbidden-action HARD-GATEs in brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan load-bearing via tool-use-time enforcement","description":"STUB epic: phase-aware PreToolUse hook + (skill,phase,forbidden-tool) registry + audited one-shot override. Recommend /dso:brainstorm refinement before sprint.","successCriteria":["sc-1","sc-2","sc-3"]},"researchFindings":[],"stories":[{"id":"63b3-7112-6dcc-4e17","title":"As a hook author, I want every forbidden-action HARD-GATE enumerated into a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) registry, so the enforcement hook has a single data source to evaluate tool calls against","description":"## Description
**What**: Enumerate every forbidden-action HARD-GATE in the brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files and encode each as a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple in a machine-readable registry that the PreToolUse hook consumes.
**Why**: The hook (draft-2) cannot decide whether to block a tool call without a data source mapping each phase to its forbidden tool/action set. This registry is the walking-skeleton data layer that the hook reads.
**Scope**:
- IN: Reading the four SKILL.md files, identifying each HARD-GATE forbidden-action statement, encoding it as a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple, writing the registry file, and a loader function that returns the forbidden set for a given (skill, phase).
- OUT: The hook that consumes the registry (draft-2); the override CLI (draft-3); any runtime tool interception.","priority":0,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["The registry file contains a (skill, phase, forbidden-tool-or-action) tuple for each forbidden-action HARD-GATE found in the brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan SKILL.md files ← Satisfies: sc-2","A loader function returns the forbidden tool/action set for a given (skill, phase) pair and returns an empty set for a pair with no forbidden actions ← Satisfies: sc-2","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the loader function and registry parsing ← Satisfies: sc-2"],"considerations":["[Maintainability] The registry must stay in sync with the SKILL.md HARD-GATEs; encode the source skill and phase so drift is auditable.","[Convention] Any new .sh file created for the loader sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation per project convention.","[External-blocker] Phase-state shape is informed by sibling-epic infra (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) get_artifacts_dir() worktree resolution and session-state tracking; this story encodes the registry only and does not depend on an in-epic story for that infra."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":[],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-2"},{"id":"63ae-1dd9-fa54-4fcc","title":"As a sub-agent operator, I want a phase-aware PreToolUse hook that blocks tool calls forbidden by the active phase, so HARD-GATEs are load-bearing during silent execution rather than only when challenged","description":"## Description
**What**: Implement a PreToolUse hook that reads the active (skill, phase) from durable session state, looks up the forbidden set in the registry (draft-1), and blocks an in-flight tool call when its tool/action class is forbidden for that phase, emitting a structured error directing the agent to complete the prerequisite phase work or surface to the user for an override.
**Why**: This is the enforcement spine of the epic — it converts documented HARD-GATEs into tool-use-time blocks. It also carries the false-positive invariant: happy-path tool calls must pass through unblocked.
**Scope**:
- IN: Reading active phase from durable session state, registry lookup, block decision, structured block error message, pass-through for non-forbidden calls, the fixture where an Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked, and a happy-path trace test covering brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows that asserts no spurious blocks.
- OUT: Registry enumeration (draft-1); the override CLI and audit trail (draft-3).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["An agent attempting Edit during brainstorm Phase 1 is blocked by the hook, with a structured error naming the active (skill, phase) and the forbidden tool ← Satisfies: sc-1","A tool call whose tool/action class is not forbidden for the active phase passes through the hook without a block ← Satisfies: sc-1","When this story is complete, the hook derives the active (skill, phase) by reading the same durable session-state artifact the brainstorm/sprint/fix-bug/implementation-plan skills already write for resume rather than a hook-private phase store, verified by a test that drives the hook from a skill-written phase artifact ← Satisfies: sc-1","A happy-path end-to-end trace for each of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan runs with the hook active and produces no spurious blocks ← Validates Closure Check: "Zero false positives on representative session-level traces of brainstorm, sprint, fix-bug, and implementation-plan flows (each runs a happy-path session end-to-end with the new hook active and produces no spurious blocks)."","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including the phase-state read, the block decision, and the pass-through path ← Satisfies: sc-1"],"considerations":["[Reliability] The false-positive trace test is the cc-1 guard; a single spurious block on any of the four happy-path flows fails the story.","[Convention] The hook .sh file sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation; non-executable hooks are silently skipped by the gate.","[Consistency] The hook reads the skills' own durable resume artifact for active (skill, phase); a hook-private phase store would drift from the skills' resume state and produce spurious or missed blocks.","[External-blocker] Session-state-aware hook installation reuses the sibling-epic (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) pattern; no in-epic depends_on is created for that outside infra."],"scopeSplitCandidate":true,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["63b3-7112-6dcc-4e17"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-1"},{"id":"cd62-e7fe-3327-44f3","title":"As a user, I want a one-shot audited dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..." command, so I can authorize a blocked tool call once without the agent self-authorizing","description":"## Description
**What**: Add a user-invoked `dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..."` command that grants a one-shot, audited override for the next blocked forbidden-action tool call, mirroring the sibling epic's dso commit-override audit-trail pattern. The agent cannot self-authorize; the override respects dso-fbky autonomous mode.
**Why**: A load-bearing block needs a sanctioned escape valve so a user can deliberately proceed past a HARD-GATE, with an audit record, without disabling the hook.
**Scope**:
- IN: The override CLI command, one-shot consumption semantics, an audit record capturing reason and timestamp, rejection of agent self-invocation, and dso-fbky autonomous-mode handling.
- OUT: The hook itself (draft-2); the registry (draft-1); abuse-detection surfacing at sprint Phase I or end-session closure.","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A user-invoked dso forbidden-action-override --reason="..." grants a single override that the next forbidden-action block consumes, after which a subsequent forbidden call is blocked again ← Satisfies: sc-3","Each override writes an audit record capturing the supplied reason and a timestamp ← Satisfies: sc-3","An override invocation that lacks a user context (agent self-authorization) is rejected and writes no override grant ← Satisfies: sc-3","When this story is complete, under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override path follows the sibling epic's pattern and is not silently self-granted to the agent, verified by a test exercising the autonomous-mode path ← Satisfies: sc-3","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, including one-shot consumption, audit-record write, and self-authorization rejection ← Satisfies: sc-3"],"considerations":["[Security] The override must reject agent self-authorization; only a user-invoked context grants it.","[Security] Under dso-fbky autonomous mode the override is not self-granted to the agent; the autonomous-mode path mirrors the sibling epic's pattern.","[External-blocker] Reuses the sibling-epic (d076-d35e, 750c-6033) dso commit-override audit-trail pattern and get_artifacts_dir() resolution; no in-epic depends_on is created for that outside infra.","[Convention] Any new .sh file for the override command sets the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["63ae-1dd9-fa54-4fcc"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-3"}],"storyDashboard":{"totalStories":3,"uiStories":0,"criticalPath":["63b3-7112-6dcc-4e17","63ae-1dd9-fa54-4fcc","cd62-e7fe-3327-44f3"]}}
